    Engine¶

    eden.engine holds Genesis engine components that upstream Genesis does not ship: code that subclasses a Genesis engine class and runs inside scene.step(). It has two parts, the audio sensors and the MochiSolver. The engine addons guide explains what belongs here and how each part plugs into stock Genesis; the physics guide covers when to use Mochi.

    Audio sensors¶

    Importing eden.engine.sensors installs every sensor below: a Genesis Sensor subclass registers itself with Genesis' sensor manager on definition, so you pass these options as SensorOptions(sensor=...) like any gs.sensors.* options. The sensors form one audio pipeline: synthesis (ActuationAudio, ContactAudio, PianoAudio), propagation (AudioContext) and rendering (SpatialAudio).

    from eden.engine.sensors import ContactAudio, SpatialAudio
from eden.options.sensors import SensorOptions

    Motor and gearbox noise¶

    Motor and gearbox noise: the synthesis stage of the audio pipeline.

    Ported from the neuroagents-lab/tactile-genesis fork, where it is a standalone AudioSource added through a Genesis-side scene.add_audio_source. Eden has no such API and does not want to add one, so the source is wrapped in a sensor: the sensor declares itself the usual way through SensorsOptions, hands its voice to :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext at build, and exposes the synthesized block through read() as a bonus — per-joint motor audio is a usable observation in its own right, which the upstream source cannot provide.

    The sound model is unchanged: each actuated DOF radiates from its joint's child link, voiced by a velocity-pitched whine (gear mesh), an idle electrical hum, velocity-scaled bearing hiss, and a click on direction reversal, with loudness driven by joint torque and mechanical power.

    Provenance

    Ported from neuroagents-lab/tactile-genesis @ 3023bcd (Genesis/genesis/engine/audio/actuation_source.py).

    Deviations from upstream: a sensor rather than a standalone source (above); entity_idx is validated against the scene rather than at options construction, since Eden injects it at build; every oscillator partial is kept below Nyquist, where upstream bounds only the whine fundamental; a gain tuple longer than n_partials raises instead of being truncated; the whine fades out below 20 Hz, where upstream's frozen oscillators turn the holding torque of a still joint into a DC offset; a block is synthesized in closed form rather than sample by sample (same signal, to float rounding); and the friction_freq / friction_bandwidth / click_freq defaults are lowered from upstream's 1200 / 800 / 3000 Hz, which the default 4 kHz audio rate cannot carry.

    Limitation: parametric synthesis, not a measured motor model. The timbre is plausible rather than calibrated to any real actuator, so treat absolute amplitudes as arbitrary units.

    Classes¶

    ActuationAudioProperties ¶

    Bases: NamedTuple

    Timbre of one joint's actuator: how a motor and gearbox sound as a function of torque and speed.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    pitch_slope

    Whine fundamental in Hz per rad/s of joint speed, bundling gear ratio and mesh teeth. The whine pitch is pitch_slope * |omega|.

    TYPE: float

    harmonic_gains

    Relative gains of the whine partials (fundamental, 2x, 3x, ...). Zero-padded to n_partials; more gains than n_partials raises at build. The whine pitch saturates where the highest partial with a non-zero gain reaches the audio rate's ceiling, so fewer partials buy a higher top pitch.

    TYPE: tuple[float, ...]

    idle_freq

    Frequency in Hz of the idle electrical hum (PWM, magnetostriction).

    TYPE: float

    idle_gain

    Hum amplitude while the motor is energized, i.e. whenever |tau| > 0. This is the static component: with torque roughly constant while a joint holds position it is a constant tone. Use idle_velocity_gain instead to keep a held joint quiet. 0 disables it.

    TYPE: float

    idle_velocity_gain

    Adds idle_velocity_gain * |omega| to the hum amplitude, so the hum's fixed-pitch lines are driven by motion rather than holding torque: quiet when still, louder when moving.

    TYPE: float

    idle_harmonic_gains

    Relative gains of the hum's partials at idle_freq. A real servo hum is harmonic-rich, so something like (1.0, 0.6, 0.4) sounds buzzy rather than like a pure sine. Same length rule as harmonic_gains.

    TYPE: tuple[float, ...]

    friction_gain

    Amplitude of the velocity-scaled bearing and friction hiss. 0 disables it.

    TYPE: float

    friction_freq

    Center frequency in Hz of the friction noise band. Like click_freq and idle_freq, the default fits the default audio rate (audio_substeps=20 at Eden's default sim_dt=0.005, a 900 Hz ceiling); a value the scene's rate cannot carry is clamped, with a warning at build if it is audible.

    TYPE: float

    friction_bandwidth

    Spectral width in Hz of the friction noise band.

    TYPE: float

    load_gain

    Whine loudness per unit |torque| (1/N·m): a loaded joint whines louder than a free-running one at the same speed. Like all of the whine it needs motion, fading out as the pitch drops below 20 Hz; a joint straining in place is voiced by idle_gain.

    TYPE: float

    power_gain

    Loudness per unit mechanical power |tau*omega| (1/W): the working-whine component.

    TYPE: float

    reversal_click_gain

    Amplitude of the click emitted when joint velocity changes sign (backlash takeup), scaled by |omega|. 0 disables it.

    TYPE: float

    click_freq

    Center frequency in Hz of the reversal click resonator.

    TYPE: float

    click_decay

    Decay rate in 1/s of the reversal click resonator.

    TYPE: float

    slew_coeff

    One-pole smoothing in (0, 1] applied to torque and velocity before synthesis, to suppress the controller's per-step ripple. 1 is no smoothing; smaller is heavier.

    TYPE: float

    ActuationAudio ¶

    Bases: RigidEntitySensorOptionsMixin['ActuationAudioSensor'], SimpleSensorOptions['ActuationAudioSensor']

    Motor noise radiated by a robot's actuated joints, and readable as a per-joint signal.

    read() returns (B, n_dofs, audio_substeps): this step's block per covered DOF, in the order the joints appear on the entity. The same blocks are registered with the scene's audio registry, so any :class:~eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio.SpatialAudio microphone hears them from the right place — each DOF radiates from its joint's child link.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    entity_idx

    Global entity index of the actuated robot. Required; motor noise needs an actuator.

    TYPE: int

    link_idx_local

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options and meaningless here: the sensor covers the whole entity and each DOF radiates from its own joint's child link. Anything but the default raises at build.
    pos_offset

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options and meaningless here: the sensor covers the whole entity and each DOF radiates from its own joint's child link. Anything but the default raises at build.
    euler_offset

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options and meaningless here: the sensor covers the whole entity and each DOF radiates from its own joint's child link. Anything but the default raises at build.
    joints

    Names of the joints to voice. None covers every joint of the entity that has DOFs. An unknown name raises at build rather than being ignored.

    TYPE: tuple[str, ...] | None

    default_properties

    Timbre applied to every covered joint that properties does not override.

    TYPE: ActuationAudioProperties

    properties

    Per-joint-name timbre overrides.

    TYPE: dict[str, ActuationAudioProperties]

    n_partials

    Number of partials in the whine and hum oscillator banks.

    TYPE: int

    audio_substeps

    Samples emitted per physics step. Must match every other audio participant in the scene.

    TYPE: int

    Examples:

    Voice an arm's motors, with a louder whine on the shoulder:

    >>> from eden.options import SensorOptions
>>> from eden.engine.sensors.actuation_audio import ActuationAudio, ActuationAudioProperties
>>> motors = SensorOptions(
...     sensor=ActuationAudio(
...         audio_substeps=20,
...         properties={"shoulder_pan_joint": ActuationAudioProperties(power_gain=0.4)},
...     ),
...     attach_entity_name="robot",
... )

    Attributes¶

    joints class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    joints: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
    default_properties class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    default_properties: ActuationAudioProperties = ActuationAudioProperties()
    properties class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    properties: dict[str, ActuationAudioProperties] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    n_partials class-attribute instance-attribute ¶
    n_partials: PositiveInt = 3
    audio_substeps class-attribute instance-attribute ¶

    def validate_scene(self, scene: "Scene"):
    """Require a real rigid entity, and refuse the link attachment this sensor would ignore.

    Runs in ``scene.add_sensor`` before the sensor is constructed, which is after Eden has injected
    ``entity_idx`` / ``link_idx_local`` from ``attach_entity_name`` / ``attach_link_name``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : Scene
        The scene the sensor is being added to.
    """
    if self.entity_idx < 0:
        gs.raise_exception(
            "ActuationAudio needs the entity whose motors it voices, but entity_idx is still -1. Set "
            "`attach_entity_name` on the enclosing eden SensorOptions (or entity_idx directly when adding the "
            "sensor through Genesis)."
        )
    super().validate_scene(scene)
    ignored = {name: getattr(self, name) for name in ("link_idx_local", "pos_offset", "euler_offset")}
    set_anyway = {name: value for name, value in ignored.items() if any(v != 0 for v in np.atleast_1d(value))}
    if set_anyway:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"ActuationAudio covers a whole entity and ignores its link attachment, but got {set_anyway}. Each "
            "DOF radiates from its own joint's child link; drop `attach_link_name` from the enclosing eden "
            "SensorOptions and leave the offsets at their defaults. Use `joints` to voice a subset."
        )

    ActuationVoice ¶

    ActuationVoice(options: ActuationAudio, solver: RigidSolver, dof_idx, emit_links, properties)

    Bases: AudioSource

    Synthesis for one :class:ActuationAudioSensor: one emission point per covered DOF.

    Owns the oscillator phases and filter memory, which persist across steps, so it is built once and then driven by :meth:emit from the audio registry each step.

    Allocate the synthesis state for the DOFs resolved by the owning sensor.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    options

    The owning sensor's options.

    TYPE: ActuationAudio

    solver

    Solver to read per-DOF torque and velocity from.

    TYPE: RigidSolver

    dof_idx

    Solver-global DOF indices to voice, in read order.

    TYPE: list[int]

    emit_links

    Solver-global index of the link each DOF radiates from, parallel to dof_idx.

    TYPE: list[int]

    properties

    Timbre of each DOF, parallel to dof_idx.

    TYPE: list[ActuationAudioProperties]

    def __init__(self, options: ActuationAudio, solver: "RigidSolver", dof_idx, emit_links, properties):
    """Allocate the synthesis state for the DOFs resolved by the owning sensor.

    Parameters
    ----------
    options : ActuationAudio
        The owning sensor's options.
    solver : RigidSolver
        Solver to read per-DOF torque and velocity from.
    dof_idx : list[int]
        Solver-global DOF indices to voice, in read order.
    emit_links : list[int]
        Solver-global index of the link each DOF radiates from, parallel to ``dof_idx``.
    properties : list[ActuationAudioProperties]
        Timbre of each DOF, parallel to ``dof_idx``.
    """
    self._options = options
    self._solver = solver
    self._sim = solver._sim

    n_emit = len(dof_idx)
    n_partials = options.n_partials
    B = self._sim._B
    K = options.audio_substeps
    self._K = K
    self._dt_sub = self._sim.dt / K
    # Keep every synthesized partial below Nyquist for the audio rate, with margin, so a fast joint
    # saturates into a scream instead of silently folding down into a low rumble.
    self._nyquist = 0.45 * 0.5 / self._dt_sub
    self._harm_mult = torch.arange(1, n_partials + 1, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    self._dof_idx = torch.tensor(dof_idx, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    self._emit_links_t = torch.tensor(emit_links, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    self._emit_offset_t = torch.zeros((B, n_emit, 3), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    def col(attr):
        return torch.tensor([getattr(p, attr) for p in properties], dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    def bank(attr):
        gains_t = torch.zeros((n_emit, n_partials), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
        for i, props in enumerate(properties):
            gains = getattr(props, attr)
            if len(gains) > n_partials:
                gs.raise_exception(
                    f"ActuationAudio: `{attr}` has {len(gains)} gains but n_partials={n_partials}, so the "
                    f"last {len(gains) - n_partials} would never sound. Raise `n_partials` or drop them."
                )
            gains_t[i, : len(gains)] = torch.tensor(gains, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
        return gains_t

    def max_fundamental(gains_t):
        # Partial p sits at p times its fundamental, so a bank's fundamental is bounded by the ceiling over
        # the multiple of its highest partial that actually sounds.
        top_multiple = ((gains_t != 0) * self._harm_mult).amax(dim=-1)
        return self._nyquist / top_multiple.clamp(min=1.0)

    def col_below(attr, ceiling, audible):
        values = col(attr)
        ceiling = torch.as_tensor(ceiling, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device).expand_as(values)
        # A band whose gain is zero never sounds, so clamping it changes nothing worth a warning.
        clamped_audibly = torch.nonzero((values > ceiling) & audible).flatten()
        if clamped_audibly.numel() > 0:
            i = int(clamped_audibly[0])
            en.logger.warning(
                f"ActuationAudio: `{attr}` of {float(values[i]):.0f} Hz exceeds what the "
                f"{1.0 / self._dt_sub:.0f} Hz audio rate can carry and is clamped to {float(ceiling[i]):.0f} Hz. "
                "Raise `audio_substeps` to keep it."
            )
        return torch.minimum(values, ceiling)

    self._harm = bank("harmonic_gains")  # (n_emit, n_partials)
    self._idle_harm = bank("idle_harmonic_gains")  # (n_emit, n_partials)
    self._max_whine_f0 = max_fundamental(self._harm)  # (n_emit,)

    self._pitch_slope = col("pitch_slope")
    self._idle_gain = col("idle_gain")
    self._idle_velocity_gain = col("idle_velocity_gain")
    self._idle_freq = col_below(
        "idle_freq", max_fundamental(self._idle_harm), (self._idle_gain != 0) | (self._idle_velocity_gain != 0)
    )
    self._friction_gain = col("friction_gain")
    self._friction_freq = col_below("friction_freq", self._nyquist, self._friction_gain != 0)
    self._friction_bw = col("friction_bandwidth").clamp(min=gs.EPS)
    self._load_gain = col("load_gain")
    self._power_gain = col("power_gain")
    self._reversal_click_gain = col("reversal_click_gain")
    self._click_freq = col_below("click_freq", self._nyquist, self._reversal_click_gain != 0)
    self._click_decay = col("click_decay").clamp(min=gs.EPS)
    self._slew = col("slew_coeff")

    # The friction band-pass and the click resonator are two-pole recurrences with constant coefficients,
    # so each block is filtered in closed form rather than sample by sample.
    self._friction_free, self._friction_forced = two_pole_block_kernels(
        *bandpass_coeffs(self._friction_freq, self._friction_bw, self._dt_sub), K
    )
    self._click_free, self._click_forced = two_pole_block_kernels(
        *resonator_coeffs(self._click_freq, self._click_decay, self._dt_sub), K
    )
    # Sample k of a block is k + 1 oscillator steps after the phase the previous block ended on.
    self._osc_steps = torch.arange(1, K + 1, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._idle_dphase = 2.0 * torch.pi * self._idle_freq.unsqueeze(-1) * self._harm_mult * self._dt_sub

    # Persistent synthesis state: oscillator phases, band-pass and resonator memory, slew filters.
    self._phase = torch.zeros((B, n_emit, n_partials), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._idle_phase = torch.zeros((B, n_emit, n_partials), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._ty1 = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._ty2 = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._ay1 = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._ay2 = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._prev_omega = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._slew_tau = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._slew_omega = torch.zeros((B, n_emit), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._block = torch.zeros((B, n_emit, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    def reset(self, envs_idx) -> None:
    """Zero the oscillator phases, filter memory, and last block for ``envs_idx``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    envs_idx : array-like | None
        Environments to reset. ``None`` resets all of them.
    """
    idx = slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx
    for tensor in (
        self._phase,
        self._idle_phase,
        self._ty1,
        self._ty2,
        self._ay1,
        self._ay2,
        self._prev_omega,
        self._slew_tau,
        self._slew_omega,
        self._block,
    ):
        tensor[idx] = 0.0

    def emit(self) -> None:
    """Synthesize this step's block from the current per-DOF torque and velocity."""
    solver = self._solver
    if self._block.numel() == 0:
        return
    B, n_emit, K = self._block.shape
    dt_sub = self._dt_sub

    tau = solver.get_dofs_control_force(self._dof_idx)
    omega = solver.get_dofs_velocity(self._dof_idx)
    if solver.n_envs == 0:
        tau, omega = tau[None], omega[None]  # (B, n_emit)

    # One-pole slew limit denoises the controller's per-step torque and velocity ripple, which would
    # otherwise be audible as a buzz at the control rate rather than as motor noise.
    self._slew_tau += self._slew * (tau - self._slew_tau)
    self._slew_omega += self._slew * (omega - self._slew_omega)
    tau_f, omega_f = self._slew_tau, self._slew_omega

    load_amp = self._load_gain * tau_f.abs() + self._power_gain * (tau_f * omega_f).abs()  # (B, n_emit)
    f0 = torch.minimum(self._pitch_slope * omega_f.abs(), self._max_whine_f0)
    # A joint holding still under load has torque but no pitch: its oscillators freeze mid-cycle, and
    # `load_gain * |tau|` times a frozen sine is a DC offset that steps whenever the torque does — a thump, and
    # headroom lost to something inaudible. Gear mesh only sounds while the gears turn, so fade the whine out
    # as its pitch drops below hearing.
    load_amp = load_amp * (f0 / _AUDIBLE_FLOOR_HZ).clamp(max=1.0)
    # Static (torque-on) hum floor plus a motion-driven term, so the hum tracks joint speed instead
    # of droning constantly while the joint merely holds position.
    idle_amp = self._idle_gain * (tau_f.abs() > 1e-3).to(gs.tc_float) + self._idle_velocity_gain * omega_f.abs()
    friction_amp = self._friction_gain * omega_f.abs()
    # Reversal click: velocity changed sign since last step, i.e. the gear backlash took up.
    sign_flip = (torch.sign(omega_f) * torch.sign(self._prev_omega)) < 0.0
    click_kick = self._reversal_click_gain * omega_f.abs() * sign_flip.to(gs.tc_float)

    # Oscillator banks: every sample's phase at once, (B, n_emit, n_partials, K), summed over partials.
    dphase = 2.0 * torch.pi * f0.unsqueeze(-1) * self._harm_mult * dt_sub  # (B, n_emit, n_partials)
    whine_phase = self._phase.unsqueeze(-1) + dphase.unsqueeze(-1) * self._osc_steps
    idle_phase = self._idle_phase.unsqueeze(-1) + self._idle_dphase.unsqueeze(-1) * self._osc_steps
    whine = load_amp.unsqueeze(-1) * (self._harm.unsqueeze(-1) * torch.sin(whine_phase)).sum(dim=2)
    idle = idle_amp.unsqueeze(-1) * (self._idle_harm.unsqueeze(-1) * torch.sin(idle_phase)).sum(dim=2)

    # Two-pole filters in closed form (see `two_pole_block_kernels`): the memory ringing on, plus the
    # response to this block's drive. Friction is driven by noise on every sample, the click by one kick
    # on the first.
    noise = torch.randn((B, n_emit, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    friction_memory = torch.stack((self._ty1, self._ty2), dim=-1)  # (B, n_emit, 2)
    friction = torch.einsum("ekm,bem->bek", self._friction_free, friction_memory) + torch.einsum(
        "ekj,bej->bek", self._friction_forced, friction_amp.unsqueeze(-1) * noise
    )
    click_memory = torch.stack((self._ay1, self._ay2), dim=-1)
    click = torch.einsum("ekm,bem->bek", self._click_free, click_memory) + (
        self._click_forced[:, :, 0] * click_kick.unsqueeze(-1)
    )

    self._phase.copy_(whine_phase[..., -1] % (2.0 * torch.pi))
    self._idle_phase.copy_(idle_phase[..., -1] % (2.0 * torch.pi))
    # The filters' memory is the block's last two outputs; a one-sample block keeps one sample of the old.
    friction_tail = torch.cat((self._ty1.unsqueeze(-1), friction), dim=-1)
    click_tail = torch.cat((self._ay1.unsqueeze(-1), click), dim=-1)
    self._ty1.copy_(friction_tail[..., -1])
    self._ty2.copy_(friction_tail[..., -2])
    self._ay1.copy_(click_tail[..., -1])
    self._ay2.copy_(click_tail[..., -2])
    self._prev_omega.copy_(omega_f)
    self._block.copy_(whine + idle + friction + click)

    def build(self):
    """Build this sensor's voice and register it with the scene's audio registry."""
    super().build()

    context = self._shared_context
    self._voice = ActuationVoice(
        self._options,
        self._manager._sim.rigid_solver,
        self._dof_idx,
        self._emit_links,
        self._properties,
    )
    context.register(self._voice, type(self._options).__name__)

    sm = self._shared_metadata
    sm.voices.append(self._voice)
    sm.cache_offsets.append(self._cache_offset)

    Functions:¶

    Contact sound¶

    Contact microphone: the sound of a link touching, tapping and scraping the things around it.

    A source-filter model. The filter is the struck object — a bank of damped modal oscillators whose frequencies and decay rates are its material signature (metal rings long and high, wood thuds). The source is the contact: a tap is an impulse into the bank, sliding is force- and speed-scaled noise shaped by the surface roughness, and a hard tap adds a short high click. The timbre is keyed by the material of the link being struck, not the link carrying the sensor: a fingertip sounds like whatever it touches.

    Like :mod:~eden.engine.sensors.actuation_audio the synthesis lives in an :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioSource, so :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext drives it on every simulation step and any :class:~eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio.SpatialAudio microphone hears it from the sensor's link. read() exposes the same block as a structure-borne vibration signal.

    Provenance

    Ported from neuroagents-lab/tactile-genesis @ 3023bcd (Genesis/genesis/engine/sensors/contact_audio.py and Genesis/genesis/options/sensors/audio.py). The fused block kernel and the contact-driver math are upstream's.

    Deviations from upstream:

    • Synthesis runs from AudioContext.update rather than the sensor's own update hook. Eden skips sensor updates on intermediate decimation sub-steps, and a tap lasts one simulation step — synthesized from the sensor hook, three taps in four would never sound at decimation=4.
    • Materials are keyed by Eden scene names ("table", "robot/hand") instead of solver link indices, which a declarative config cannot know; an unknown name raises at build. Two sensors giving one name different materials raise instead of the later one winning.
    • Not ported: ContactAudioProperties.from_mesh and the strike-location mode-shape tables it fills (they need upstream's genesis.utils.modal_analysis, which stock Genesis does not have), and the active-acoustic ExcitationSignal emitter.
    • accel_noise_freq defaults to 800 Hz, not 5000 Hz, which the default 4 kHz audio rate cannot carry; a mode or click the rate cannot carry warns at build when it would have sounded.

    Limitations: one dominant contact per sensor link drives the timbre; slip speed is taken between link origins, ignoring the lever arm of a rotating body; radiation is a point source at the sensor link with no directivity.

    Classes¶

    ContactAudioProperties ¶

    Bases: NamedTuple

    How an object sounds when something touches it: its resonances, and the roughness of its surface.

    Metal-like materials have high modes that decay slowly (a long ring); wood-like ones have lower modes that decay fast, and a stronger roughness source.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    modal_freqs

    Resonant mode frequencies in Hz. Fewer than the sensor's n_modes is zero-padded; more raises. A mode the audio rate cannot carry is silenced, with a warning at build.

    TYPE: tuple[float, ...]

    modal_decays

    Amplitude decay rate of each mode in 1/s. Large is a thud, small a long ring. Same length as modal_freqs.

    TYPE: tuple[float, ...]

    modal_gains

    Output weight of each mode. Same length as modal_freqs.

    TYPE: tuple[float, ...]

    roughness_gain

    Amplitude of the sliding-texture noise, scaled at runtime by normal force and slip speed. 0 is a smooth, silent slide.

    TYPE: float

    roughness_spatial_freq

    Surface bumps per meter. The scrape's pitch is roughness_spatial_freq * slip_speed Hz, so sliding faster raises it.

    TYPE: float

    roughness_bandwidth

    Spectral width in Hz of the scrape around that pitch. Several hundred Hz gives a noisy "shhh"; a narrow band an unrealistic tone.

    TYPE: float

    impact_gain

    Scale of the impulse a tap injects into the modal bank.

    TYPE: float

    impact_threshold

    Force jump in N per simulation step that counts as a tap. A tap fires only when the force crosses this from below, so the force ripple of a sustained slide does not re-ping the modes into a buzz.

    TYPE: float

    contact_damping

    Extra modal decay in 1/s while in contact: a finger pressing on an object deadens it, so the free ring-down is only heard after release.

    TYPE: float

    contact_damping_per_force

    Further in-contact decay per newton of normal force, in 1/(s·N): a firm press deadens the ring more than a light touch (Zheng & James 2011).

    TYPE: float

    accel_noise_gain

    Amplitude of the short high click a tap adds on top of the ring-down: the Hertzian contact transient of small hard objects, which the modal bank misses. 0 disables it.

    TYPE: float

    accel_noise_freq

    Center frequency in Hz of the click. Clamped to what the audio rate can carry, with a warning at build if the click is audible.

    TYPE: float

    accel_noise_decay

    Decay rate in 1/s of the click. Large is short and snappy.

    TYPE: float

    ContactAudio ¶

    Bases: RigidSensorOptionsMixin['ContactAudioSensor'], SimpleSensorOptions['ContactAudioSensor']

    The sound of one link's contacts, keyed by the material of whatever it touches.

    read() returns (B, audio_substeps): this step's block of the structure-borne vibration at the link. The same block is registered with the scene's audio registry, radiating from the link (plus pos_offset), so any :class:~eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio.SpatialAudio microphone hears it.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    entity_idx

    Global entity index of the body carrying the sensor. Required; Eden fills it from attach_entity_name.

    TYPE: int

    link_idx_local

    Local index of the link whose contacts are voiced. Eden fills it from attach_link_name.

    TYPE: int

    pos_offset

    Where on the link the sound radiates from, in the link's frame.

    TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

    euler_offset

    Accepted for parity with other link-attached sensors; a point source has no direction.

    TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

    properties

    Material of the things this link may touch, by Eden scene name: "table" covers every link of that entity, "robot/hand" one link. Merged across every ContactAudio sensor in the scene; an unknown name raises at build, and so does one name given two different materials.

    TYPE: dict[str, ContactAudioProperties]

    default_properties

    Material of every link properties does not name. None leaves contacts with them silent.

    TYPE: ContactAudioProperties | None

    audio_substeps

    Samples emitted per physics step. Must match every other audio participant in the scene; the sample rate is audio_substeps / sim_dt. Real materials ring at kHz, so expect to raise this well above the default.

    TYPE: int

    n_modes

    Size of the modal bank. Must be the same on every ContactAudio sensor in the scene.

    TYPE: int

    velocity_gate_ref

    If positive, scale the output by motion / (motion + velocity_gate_ref), where motion is the speed of the sensor's own link in m/s: a body at rest goes quiet, which suppresses the clicks of a resting contact re-settling. 0 disables the gate.

    TYPE: float

    velocity_gate_ang_weight

    Meters per radian converting the link's angular speed into motion, roughly the body's radius.

    TYPE: float

    velocity_gate_smooth

    One-pole smoothing in (0, 1] of the gate across simulation steps, so it cannot click by itself. 1 is no smoothing.

    TYPE: float

    Examples:

    A fingertip that hears what it touches:

    >>> from eden.options import SensorOptions
>>> from eden.engine.sensors.contact_audio import ContactAudio, ContactAudioProperties
>>> steel = ContactAudioProperties(modal_freqs=(1200.0, 2900.0), modal_decays=(6.0, 9.0), modal_gains=(1.0, 0.6))
>>> finger = SensorOptions(
...     sensor=ContactAudio(audio_substeps=80, properties={"bowl": steel}),
...     attach_entity_name="robot",
...     attach_link_name="left_finger",
... )

    validate_scene ¶

    def validate_scene(self, scene: "Scene"):
    """Require a link to listen on, and that every named material exists in the scene.

    Runs in ``scene.add_sensor``, after Eden has injected ``entity_idx`` / ``link_idx_local``. Entities are
    all added before any sensor, so a name that does not resolve here never will.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : Scene
        The scene the sensor is being added to.
    """
    if self.entity_idx < 0:
        gs.raise_exception(
            "ContactAudio needs the link whose contacts it voices, but entity_idx is still -1. Set "
            "`attach_entity_name` (and usually `attach_link_name`) on the enclosing eden SensorOptions."
        )
    super().validate_scene(scene)
    for key in self.properties:
        _material_links(scene.entities, key)

    def __init__(
    self, solver: "RigidSolver", metadata: "ContactAudioSensorMetadata", n_modes: int, audio_substeps: int
):
    """Create an empty voice; sensors join through :meth:`add_sensor`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    solver : RigidSolver
        Solver to read contacts and link velocities from.
    metadata : ContactAudioSensorMetadata
        The sensor class's shared metadata, read for each sensor's link and radiation offset.
    n_modes : int
        Size of the modal bank.
    audio_substeps : int
        Samples per simulation step.
    """
    self._solver = solver
    self._metadata = metadata
    self._n_modes = n_modes
    self._K = audio_substeps
    self._dt_sub = solver._sim.dt / audio_substeps
    self._band_edge = _BAND_EDGE * 0.5 / self._dt_sub
    # One-pole DC-blocking high-pass: R = 1 - 2*pi*fc/fs.
    self._hp_r = max(0.0, 1.0 - 2.0 * torch.pi * _DC_BLOCK_HZ * self._dt_sub)

    self._materials: dict[str, ContactAudioProperties] = {}
    self._link_material = torch.full((solver.n_links,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=gs.device)
    self._table: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}

    def state(*shape):
        return torch.zeros((solver._sim._B, 0, *shape), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    # Persistent synthesis state, one column per sensor. `cur_*` latch the *free* coefficients of the last
    # material touched, so a released mode keeps ringing down with that material's own decay.
    self._modal_y = state(n_modes, 2)
    self._cur_a1, self._cur_a2, self._cur_gains = state(n_modes), state(n_modes), state(n_modes)
    self._tex_y, self._acc_y, self._hp_state = state(2), state(2), state(2)
    self._prev_force, self._gate_state = state(), state()
    self._block = state(audio_substeps)
    # Per-sensor velocity gate, (n_sensors,).
    self._gate_ref = torch.zeros((0,), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._gate_ang_w = torch.zeros((0,), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._gate_smooth = torch.zeros((0,), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._has_gate = False

    def add_sensor(self, options: ContactAudio, scene_entities) -> None:
    """Grow every state tensor by one sensor column and merge in the sensor's materials.

    Parameters
    ----------
    options : ContactAudio
        The joining sensor's options.
    scene_entities : list
        The scene's Genesis entities, for resolving material names to links.
    """
    for key, props in options.materials().items():
        if self._materials.setdefault(key, props) != props:
            name = f"material '{key}'" if key else "default_properties"
            gs.raise_exception(
                f"ContactAudio {name} is declared twice with different values. Materials are shared by every "
                "ContactAudio sensor in the scene; declare each one once, or identically."
            )
    self._rebuild_material_table(scene_entities)

    for attr in self._STATE:
        tensor = getattr(self, attr)
        setattr(self, attr, torch.cat((tensor, tensor.new_zeros((tensor.shape[0], 1, *tensor.shape[2:]))), dim=1))
    self._gate_ref = concat_with_tensor(self._gate_ref, options.velocity_gate_ref)
    self._gate_ang_w = concat_with_tensor(self._gate_ang_w, options.velocity_gate_ang_weight)
    self._gate_smooth = concat_with_tensor(self._gate_smooth, options.velocity_gate_smooth)
    self._has_gate = self._has_gate or options.velocity_gate_ref > 0.0

    def reset(self, envs_idx) -> None:
    """Silence the resonators and forget the last contact for ``envs_idx``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    envs_idx : array-like | None
        Environments to reset. ``None`` resets all of them.
    """
    idx = slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx
    for attr in self._STATE:
        getattr(self, attr)[idx] = 0.0

    def emit(self) -> None:
    """Synthesize this step's block from the contacts on each sensor link."""
    solver, table = self._solver, self._table
    B, n_sensors, n_modes = self._modal_y.shape[:3]
    if n_sensors == 0:
        return
    if not self._materials:
        # Every sensor has joined by the first emit, which runs inside env.build(), so this still fails at build.
        gs.raise_exception(
            "No ContactAudio sensor in the scene declares a material, so none of them could ever sound. Set "
            "`properties` (by Eden scene name) or `default_properties` on at least one."
        )
    K, dt_sub = self._K, self._dt_sub
    sensor_links = self._metadata.links_idx.long()  # (S,)

    # --- 1) Contact drivers, constant over the block, aggregated per sensor link.
    contacts = solver.collider.get_contacts(as_tensor=True, to_torch=True, keep_batch_dim=True)
    force, normal = contacts["force"], contacts["normal"]  # (B, C, 3)
    link_a, link_b = contacts["link_a"].long(), contacts["link_b"].long()  # (B, C), -1 where padded
    n_contacts = link_a.shape[-1]

    zeros = torch.zeros((B, n_sensors), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    if n_contacts == 0:
        # Nothing touching: no drive, and the modal bank rings down with its latched free coefficients.
        f_normal = zeros
        a1, a2, gains = self._cur_a1, self._cur_a2, self._cur_gains
        # Zero feedback lets the texture and click memory die at once; both are sub-millisecond anyway.
        impulse = modal_drive = tex_amp = accel_kick = at1 = at2 = aa1 = aa2 = zeros
    else:
        is_a = link_a[:, None, :] == sensor_links[None, :, None]  # (B, S, C)
        is_b = link_b[:, None, :] == sensor_links[None, :, None]
        involved = is_a | is_b
        any_contact = involved.any(dim=2)  # (B, S)

        # Total contact force on the sensor link (Newton's third law: +force when the sensor is link_b).
        orient = is_b.to(gs.tc_float) - is_a.to(gs.tc_float)
        f_normal = (orient[..., None] * force[:, None]).sum(dim=2).norm(dim=-1)  # (B, S)

        # The contact with the largest force speaks for the link: its counterpart is the struck material.
        primary = torch.where(involved, force.norm(dim=-1)[:, None], 0.0).argmax(dim=2)  # (B, S), into C
        other = torch.where(is_a, link_b[:, None, :], link_a[:, None, :])  # (B, S, C)
        struck = other.gather(2, primary[..., None]).squeeze(-1).clamp(min=0)  # (B, S)
        primary_normal = normal[:, None].expand(B, n_sensors, n_contacts, 3)
        primary_normal = primary_normal.gather(2, primary[..., None, None].expand(B, n_sensors, 1, 3)).squeeze(2)

        # Slip: the tangential part of the two link origins' relative velocity.
        links_vel = solver.get_links_vel()
        if solver.n_envs == 0:
            links_vel = links_vel[None]  # (B, n_links, 3)
        v_rel = links_vel[:, sensor_links] - links_vel.gather(1, struck[..., None].expand(B, n_sensors, 3))
        v_tan = v_rel - (v_rel * primary_normal).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) * primary_normal
        slip = v_tan.norm(dim=-1) * any_contact

        material = self._link_material[struck]  # (B, S), -1 where the struck link has no material
        valid = any_contact & (material >= 0)
        validf = valid.to(gs.tc_float)
        material = material.clamp(min=0)

        # Two coefficient sets per mode. While pressed, the finger damps the object (a floor plus a term per
        # newton), so a slide does not ring into a tone; the free decay alone is latched for after release.
        theta = 2.0 * torch.pi * table["freqs"][material] * dt_sub  # (B, S, M)
        decays = table["decays"][material]
        pressed = table["contact_damping"][material] + table["damp_per_force"][material] * f_normal
        free_r = torch.exp(-decays * dt_sub)
        pressed_r = torch.exp(-(decays + pressed[..., None]) * dt_sub)

        touching = valid[..., None]
        a1 = torch.where(touching, 2.0 * pressed_r * torch.cos(theta), self._cur_a1)
        a2 = torch.where(touching, pressed_r * pressed_r, self._cur_a2)
        gains = torch.where(touching, table["gains"][material], self._cur_gains)
        self._cur_a1.copy_(torch.where(touching, 2.0 * free_r * torch.cos(theta), self._cur_a1))
        self._cur_a2.copy_(torch.where(touching, free_r * free_r, self._cur_a2))
        self._cur_gains.copy_(gains)

        # A tap fires only when the force crosses the threshold from below. The solver's contact force ripples
        # during a slide; gating on the jump alone would inject an impulse every step, a buzz at the step rate.
        d_force = (f_normal - self._prev_force).clamp(min=0.0)
        threshold = table["impact_thresh"][material]
        tap = d_force * ((d_force > threshold) & (self._prev_force <= threshold)) * validf
        impulse = table["impact_gain"][material] * tap
        accel_kick = table["accel_gain"][material] * tap
        click_r = torch.exp(-table["accel_decay"][material] * dt_sub)
        aa1 = 2.0 * click_r * torch.cos(2.0 * torch.pi * table["accel_freq"][material] * dt_sub)
        aa2 = click_r * click_r

        # Sliding texture: a broadband scrape at the slip pitch, plus the same noise into the (damped) modal
        # bank, so the object's resonances color the scrape as formants instead of ringing as a tone.
        tex_amp = table["rough_gain"][material] * f_normal * slip * validf
        modal_drive = _MODAL_NOISE_FRAC * tex_amp
        tex_freq = (table["rough_sf"][material] * slip).clamp(max=self._band_edge)
        tex_r = torch.exp(-torch.pi * table["rough_bw"][material] * dt_sub)
        at1 = 2.0 * tex_r * torch.cos(2.0 * torch.pi * tex_freq * dt_sub)
        at2 = tex_r * tex_r

    # --- 2) The block itself, in one fused kernel over (env, sensor).
    tex_noise = torch.randn((B, n_sensors, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    modal_noise = torch.randn((B, n_sensors, n_modes, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    out = torch.empty((B, n_sensors, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    _kernel_synthesize_block(
        a1.contiguous(),
        a2.contiguous(),
        gains.contiguous(),
        modal_drive.contiguous(),
        modal_noise,
        tex_noise,
        impulse.contiguous(),
        at1.contiguous(),
        at2.contiguous(),
        aa1.contiguous(),
        aa2.contiguous(),
        tex_amp.contiguous(),
        accel_kick.contiguous(),
        self._modal_y,
        self._tex_y,
        self._acc_y,
        self._hp_state,
        out,
        float(self._hp_r),
    )
    self._prev_force.copy_(f_normal)

    # --- 3) Optional gate on the sensor link's own motion, so a body at rest goes quiet.
    if self._has_gate:
        links_idx = self._metadata.links_idx
        links_vel, links_ang = solver.get_links_vel(links_idx), solver.get_links_ang(links_idx)
        if solver.n_envs == 0:
            links_vel, links_ang = links_vel[None], links_ang[None]
        motion = links_vel.norm(dim=-1) + self._gate_ang_w * links_ang.norm(dim=-1)  # (B, S)
        target = motion / (motion + self._gate_ref).clamp(min=gs.EPS)
        self._gate_state += self._gate_smooth * (target - self._gate_state)
        out = out * torch.where(self._gate_ref > 0.0, self._gate_state, 1.0)[..., None]

    self._block.copy_(out)

    def build(self):
    """Create the class's voice if this is its first sensor, and add this sensor's column to it."""
    super().build()

    sm, context, options = self._shared_metadata, self._shared_context, self._options
    if sm.voice is None:
        sm.voice = ContactVoice(sm.solver, sm, options.n_modes, options.audio_substeps)
        context.register(sm.voice, type(options).__name__)
    else:
        context.require_audio_substeps(options.audio_substeps, type(options).__name__)
        if options.n_modes != sm.voice._n_modes:
            gs.raise_exception(
                f"ContactAudio declares n_modes={options.n_modes} but the scene's other ContactAudio sensors use "
                f"n_modes={sm.voice._n_modes}. They share one modal bank, so n_modes must agree."
            )
    sm.voice.add_sensor(options, self._manager._sim.entities)

    Functions:¶

    Piano keyboard¶

    The sound of a piano keyboard: struck strings, voiced from the motion of the keys.

    A keyboard entity (:class:~eden.options.objects.piano.Piano) is only hinges and springs. This sensor turns the motion of those hinges into notes and publishes them to the scene's audio registry, so any :class:~eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio.SpatialAudio microphone hears the instrument, and read() returns the same signal directly.

    The model is a piano action reduced to its three audible events:

    • Strike. When a key travels past strike_fraction of its stroke the hammer is thrown, and how loud the note is depends on how fast the key was moving at that moment, nothing else. A key pressed slowly enough makes no sound, as on the real instrument.
    • Ring. The string is a bank of partials at n * f0 * sqrt(1 + inharmonicity * n**2), each an exponentially decaying sinusoid; higher partials and higher notes die faster. While the key stays down the damper is off the string and the note rings on.
    • Damp. When the key comes back up past release_fraction the damper falls and the note is gone in a few tens of milliseconds, unless the sustain pedal (:meth:PianoAudioSensor.set_sustain) is down.

    What a key is touched by plays no part, which is the difference from :class:~eden.engine.sensors.contact_audio.ContactAudio: there the contact force is the excitation and staying in contact damps the ring, the opposite of both on a piano.

    Each partial is held as a rotating phasor rather than as a two-pole recurrence, so a block is linear in the phasors: one matrix product against precomputed tables of decay envelope times sine and cosine, exact to rounding at any pitch. The recurrence would do badly here: at 27.5 Hz and a one-second decay its two state samples differ in the fifth digit, and float32 would turn that into noise. It also makes the damper free: lifting or dropping it only swaps the envelope table.

    RoboPianist, where the keyboard's dimensions come from, does not synthesize sound: it sends note-on/off events to a MIDI synthesizer with every strike at full velocity. Its "key is down" test, within half a degree of the joint limit, is about 87% of a white key's stroke, which is where strike_fraction defaults.

    Limitation: parametric synthesis, not a sampled instrument. It is recognizably a struck string with the right pitch, dynamics and damping, not a grand piano; amplitudes are arbitrary units.

    Classes¶

    PianoAudio ¶

    Bases: RigidEntitySensorOptionsMixin['PianoAudioSensor'], SimpleSensorOptions['PianoAudioSensor']

    The sound of a keyboard entity, from the motion of its key joints.

    read() returns (B, audio_substeps): this step's block of the whole instrument. The same block is registered with the scene's audio registry and radiates from the keyboard's base link.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    entity_idx

    Global entity index of the keyboard. Required.

    TYPE: int

    link_idx_local

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options. pos_offset moves the point the sound radiates from, in the base link's frame; the other two are meaningless here and anything but the default raises at build.
    pos_offset

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options. pos_offset moves the point the sound radiates from, in the base link's frame; the other two are meaningless here and anything but the default raises at build.
    euler_offset

    Inherited from Genesis' link-attached sensor options. pos_offset moves the point the sound radiates from, in the base link's frame; the other two are meaningless here and anything but the default raises at build.
    key_notes

    The keys to voice and what each plays: key joint name to MIDI note number. Its order is the column order of :attr:PianoAudioSensor.keys_down. None voices every single-DOF joint of the entity, in order, as a chromatic run from lowest_midi_note, which is right for :class:~eden.options.objects.piano.Piano. To voice only some of its keys, name each with its own note, e.g. {key_joint_name(key): LOWEST_MIDI_NOTE + key for key in keys}. An unknown name raises at build.

    TYPE: dict[str, int] | None

    lowest_midi_note

    MIDI note number of the entity's first key joint when key_notes is None; 21 is the A0 of an 88-key piano. Key i plays note lowest_midi_note + i, in equal temperament like every note. Changing it alongside key_notes raises, since the notes are then given there.

    TYPE: int

    tuning

    Frequency of A4 (MIDI note 69), in Hz.

    TYPE: float

    strike_fraction

    Fraction of a key's stroke at which the hammer is thrown.

    TYPE: float

    release_fraction

    Fraction of the stroke below which a returning key drops its damper. Must be below strike_fraction; the gap between them is what stops a key hovering at the strike point from re-striking.

    TYPE: float

    velocity_ref

    Key speed at the strike, in rad/s, that gives a full-scale note. Loudness is proportional to speed up to here and saturates above. A forte stroke takes a white key through its 10 mm in about 20 ms, 3 rad/s.

    TYPE: float

    n_partials

    Partials per string.

    TYPE: int

    inharmonicity

    String stiffness coefficient B: partial n sits at n * f0 * sqrt(1 + B * n**2), slightly sharp of harmonic. 0 is an ideal string.

    TYPE: float

    partial_rolloff

    Partial n starts at amplitude n ** -partial_rolloff. Larger is mellower.

    TYPE: float

    ring_decay

    Amplitude decay rate, in 1/s, of the fundamental of A4 while the damper is up.

    TYPE: float

    decay_pitch_exponent

    Decay rates scale with (f0 / tuning) ** decay_pitch_exponent: a treble string dies sooner than a bass one.

    TYPE: float

    partial_decay_growth

    Partial n decays 1 + partial_decay_growth * (n - 1) times faster than the fundamental, which is what makes a note mellow as it rings.

    TYPE: float

    damped_decay

    Decay rate, in 1/s, once the damper is down. Partials that already decay faster keep their own rate.

    TYPE: float

    audio_substeps

    Samples emitted per physics step. Must match every other audio participant in the scene. The default of 80 is a 16 kHz rate at Eden's default sim_dt=0.005, which carries every fundamental on the keyboard; the 20 of the other audio sensors' defaults would leave everything above A5 mute.

    TYPE: int

    Examples:

    def validate_scene(self, scene: "Scene"):
    """Require a real rigid entity, and refuse the link attachment this sensor would ignore.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : Scene
        The scene the sensor is being added to.
    """
    if self.entity_idx < 0:
        gs.raise_exception(
            "PianoAudio needs the keyboard entity it voices, but entity_idx is still -1. Set "
            "`attach_entity_name` on the enclosing eden SensorOptions (or entity_idx directly when adding the "
            "sensor through Genesis)."
        )
    super().validate_scene(scene)
    ignored = {name: getattr(self, name) for name in ("link_idx_local", "euler_offset")}
    set_anyway = {name: value for name, value in ignored.items() if any(v != 0 for v in np.atleast_1d(value))}
    if set_anyway:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"PianoAudio voices a whole keyboard and radiates from its base link, but got {set_anyway}. Drop "
            "`attach_link_name` from the enclosing eden SensorOptions; use `pos_offset` to move the point the "
            "sound comes from."
        )

    def __init__(
    self, options: PianoAudio, solver: "RigidSolver", dof_idx: list[int], notes: list[int], emit_link: int
):
    """Allocate the strings of the keys resolved by the owning sensor.

    Parameters
    ----------
    options : PianoAudio
        The owning sensor's options.
    solver : RigidSolver
        Solver to read the key positions from.
    dof_idx : list[int]
        Solver-global DOF index of each key.
    notes : list[int]
        MIDI note number each key plays, parallel to ``dof_idx``.
    emit_link : int
        Solver-global index of the link the instrument radiates from.
    """
    self._solver = solver
    sim = solver._sim
    B = sim._B
    K = options.audio_substeps
    n_keys = len(dof_idx)
    n_partials = options.n_partials
    self._K = K
    self._dt = sim.dt
    dt_sub = sim.dt / K
    # A sampled sine is exact at any pitch below Nyquist, so the strings run up to 90% of it. The other sources
    # stop at 45%, which their two-pole filters need and these oscillators do not.
    band_edge = 0.9 * 0.5 / dt_sub

    self._dof_idx = torch.tensor(dof_idx, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    self._emit_links_t = torch.tensor([emit_link], dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    offset = torch.tensor(options.pos_offset, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._emit_offset_t = offset.expand(B, 1, 3).contiguous()
    self._velocity_ref = options.velocity_ref

    lower, upper = solver.get_dofs_limit(self._dof_idx)
    lower, upper = lower.reshape(-1, n_keys)[0], upper.reshape(-1, n_keys)[0]
    unbounded = torch.nonzero(~torch.isfinite(upper - lower) | (upper <= lower)).flatten()
    if unbounded.numel() > 0:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"PianoAudio: key {int(unbounded[0])} (DOF {dof_idx[int(unbounded[0])]}) has no finite joint range, so "
            "there is no stroke to place the strike point on. Every key joint needs a lower and an upper limit."
        )
    self._strike_at = lower + options.strike_fraction * (upper - lower)  # (n_keys,)
    self._release_at = lower + options.release_fraction * (upper - lower)

    # Everything below is built in float64 and only the finished tables are cast down.
    f64 = torch.float64
    notes_t = torch.tensor(notes, dtype=f64, device=gs.device)
    f0 = options.tuning * 2.0 ** ((notes_t - 69.0) / 12.0)  # (n_keys,)
    n = torch.arange(1, n_partials + 1, dtype=f64, device=gs.device)
    freq = f0[:, None] * n * torch.sqrt(1.0 + options.inharmonicity * n * n)  # (n_keys, n_partials)
    ring = (
        options.ring_decay
        * (f0[:, None] / options.tuning) ** options.decay_pitch_exponent
        * (1.0 + options.partial_decay_growth * (n - 1.0))
    )
    damped = ring.clamp(min=options.damped_decay)

    carried = freq < band_edge
    mute = ~carried[:, 0]
    if mute.any():
        en.logger.warning(
            f"PianoAudio: the {1.0 / dt_sub:.0f} Hz audio rate carries nothing above {band_edge:.0f} Hz, so "
            f"{int(mute.sum())} of {n_keys} keys are mute, from MIDI note {int(notes_t[mute].min())} "
            f"({float(f0[mute].min()):.0f} Hz) up. Raise `audio_substeps` to hear them."
        )
    # A partial the rate cannot carry is dropped rather than folded down to a wrong pitch.
    self._gain = (n**-options.partial_rolloff * carried).to(gs.tc_float)  # (n_keys, n_partials)

    steps = torch.arange(1, K + 1, dtype=f64, device=gs.device)
    phase = 2.0 * torch.pi * freq[..., None] * dt_sub * steps  # (n_keys, n_partials, K)
    oscillation = torch.stack((torch.sin(phase), torch.cos(phase)), dim=2)  # (n_keys, n_partials, 2, K)
    ring_env = torch.exp(-ring[..., None] * dt_sub * steps)
    damped_env = torch.exp(-damped[..., None] * dt_sub * steps)
    # Row (damper, key, partial, sin | cos) is the block one unit of that phasor component rings out under that
    # damper, so a block is the phasors times these tables; see `emit`.
    tables = torch.stack((ring_env[:, :, None] * oscillation, damped_env[:, :, None] * oscillation))
    tables = tables.reshape(-1, K).to(gs.tc_float)  # (2 * n_keys * n_partials * 2, K)
    # A float32 matmul on CUDA may run in TF32, which Eden enables by default (`eden.init(allow_tf32=True)`): 10
    # mantissa bits, a -70 dB error on every sample. Splitting both sides into a TF32-exact part and a remainder
    # and multiplying out three of the four products recovers float32 accuracy, whatever the global flag says.
    # With `_tables_lo` set, `_tables` holds only the TF32-exact part.
    self._tables, self._tables_lo = tables, None
    if gs.tc_float == torch.float32 and gs.device.type == "cuda":
        self._tables, self._tables_lo = _split_tf32(tables)
    # Carrying a phasor across a block: decay it by the envelope's last sample, turn it by the block's phase.
    self._ring_end = ring_env[..., -1].to(gs.tc_float)  # (n_keys, n_partials)
    self._damped_end = damped_env[..., -1].to(gs.tc_float)
    self._end_sin = torch.sin(phase[..., -1]).to(gs.tc_float)
    self._end_cos = torch.cos(phase[..., -1]).to(gs.tc_float)

    self._c = torch.zeros((B, n_keys, n_partials), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._s = torch.zeros((B, n_keys, n_partials), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._prev_q = torch.zeros((B, n_keys), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._prev_speed = torch.zeros((B, n_keys), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    self._down = torch.zeros((B, n_keys), dtype=torch.bool, device=gs.device)
    # An environment's first step after a reset only takes stock: a key already down was not just struck.
    self._fresh = torch.ones((B,), dtype=torch.bool, device=gs.device)
    self._sustain = torch.zeros((B,), dtype=torch.bool, device=gs.device)
    self._block = torch.zeros((B, 1, K), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    # Every block since `start_recording`, or None while not recording. `_has_recorded` separates the two
    # ways of being None — never started, and started then stopped — so neither is reported as the other.
    self._recorded: list[torch.Tensor] | None = None
    self._has_recorded = False

    def start_recording(self) -> None:
    """Start keeping every synthesized block.

    Refuses a second start while one is open, as :meth:`~eden.entities.camera.Camera.start_recording` does:
    the only thing it could do instead is throw away what the first one kept, and there is no getting that
    back.
    """
    if self._recorded is not None:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"PianoAudio: already recording, with {len(self._recorded)} block(s) kept. Starting again would "
            f"drop them. Call take_recording() to collect them and go on recording, or stop_recording() to "
            f"throw them away on purpose."
        )
    self._recorded = []
    self._has_recorded = True

    def take_recording(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return what was synthesized since the last call (or since recording started), and keep recording.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        ``(B, n_blocks * audio_substeps)`` samples, empty along the last axis if no step has run since.
    """
    if self._recorded is None:
        # Two different mistakes, and the fix differs: one call is missing, or one came too early.
        gs.raise_exception(
            "PianoAudio: take_recording() after stop_recording(), which dropped what had been kept. Take the "
            "samples before stopping, or leave the recording open."
            if self._has_recorded
            else "PianoAudio: take_recording() was called without start_recording()."
        )
    blocks, self._recorded = self._recorded, []
    if not blocks:
        return torch.zeros((self._block.shape[0], 0), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    return torch.cat(blocks, dim=-1)

    def stop_recording(self) -> None:
    """Stop keeping blocks and drop what was kept.

    Refuses when no recording is open, as :meth:`~eden.entities.camera.Camera.stop_recording` does: a stop
    with nothing to stop is a mistake in the calling loop far more often than an intent.
    """
    if self._recorded is None:
        gs.raise_exception(
            "PianoAudio: not recording, so there is nothing to stop. start_recording() opens one; "
            "take_recording() collects what it holds without closing it."
        )
    self._recorded = None

    def reset(self, envs_idx) -> None:
    """Silence every string, lift the pedal and forget which keys were down, for ``envs_idx``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    envs_idx : array-like | None
        Environments to reset. ``None`` resets all of them.
    """
    idx = slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx
    for tensor in (self._c, self._s, self._prev_speed, self._block):
        tensor[idx] = 0.0
    self._down[idx] = False
    self._sustain[idx] = False
    self._fresh[idx] = True

    def emit(self) -> None:
    """Throw the hammers of the keys that just passed their strike point, then ring every string one block."""
    q = self._solver.get_dofs_position(self._dof_idx)
    if self._solver.n_envs == 0:
        q = q[None]  # (B, n_keys)

    fresh = self._fresh[:, None]
    # The key's speed as it passed the strike point, from finite differences rather than the joint velocity,
    # which reads zero once the key has met its stop. A fast key meets it within the very step that carried it
    # past the strike point, cutting that step's travel short, so the step before counts too.
    step_speed = torch.where(fresh, 0.0, (q - self._prev_q) / self._dt)
    speed = torch.maximum(step_speed, self._prev_speed)
    self._prev_speed.copy_(step_speed)
    down = (q >= self._strike_at) | (self._down & (q > self._release_at))
    struck = down & ~self._down & ~fresh
    level = (speed / self._velocity_ref).clamp(min=0.0, max=1.0) * struck  # (B, n_keys)
    self._down.copy_(down)
    self._prev_q.copy_(q)
    self._fresh.fill_(False)

    # A strike starts each partial at a zero crossing, so the note begins without a click.
    self._c += level[..., None] * self._gain

    damped = ~(down | self._sustain[:, None])  # (B, n_keys)
    # One matrix product with the tables: each phasor goes into the rows of the envelope it rings under this
    # block, and zeros into the other's. Nothing the size of (B, n_keys, P, K) is ever built.
    phasor = torch.stack((self._c, self._s), dim=-1)  # (B, n_keys, P, 2)
    ringing = torch.where(damped[..., None, None], 0.0, phasor)
    coefficients = torch.stack((ringing, phasor - ringing), dim=1).flatten(1)  # (B, 2 * n_keys * P * 2)
    if self._tables_lo is None:
        self._block[:, 0] = coefficients @ self._tables
    else:
        hi, lo = _split_tf32(coefficients)
        self._block[:, 0] = (hi @ self._tables).addmm_(lo, self._tables).addmm_(hi, self._tables_lo)

    # Carry each phasor to the end of the block: decay it, and turn it by the phase the block covered.
    end_env = torch.where(damped[..., None], self._damped_end, self._ring_end)  # (B, n_keys, P)
    c, s = self._c, self._s
    self._c = end_env * (c * self._end_cos - s * self._end_sin)
    self._s = end_env * (c * self._end_sin + s * self._end_cos)
    if self._recorded is not None:
        self._recorded.append(self._block[:, 0].clone())

    def build(self):
    """Build this sensor's voice and register it with the scene's audio registry."""
    super().build()

    self._voice = PianoVoice(self._options, self._manager._sim.rigid_solver, dof_idx, notes, base_link)
    self._shared_context.register(self._voice, type(self._options).__name__)

    start_recording ¶
    start_recording() -> None

    Start keeping every block the strings synthesize, one per simulation step.

    read() returns the block of the latest simulation step only, so a loop that steps the environment once per control step (decimation simulation steps) reads one block in decimation. A recording has them all: it is how to listen to a policy that acts at 20 Hz. The signal is the instrument's own, before any microphone's distance and delay.

    Unlike :meth:~eden.entities.camera.Camera.start_recording, which streams to a file, this holds what it keeps in memory for every environment at once — num_envs * audio_substeps floats a simulation step, 65 MB/s at 1024 environments and the default 80 substeps. :meth:take_recording empties it, so a loop that drains each step holds one step's worth; one that never drains grows without bound. Starting a second recording while one is open raises rather than dropping what it holds, and a reset does not cut the recording: episodes are concatenated, at a different sample in each row.

    Functions:¶

    Audio sources and propagation¶

    The audio source registry and delay line every Eden audio sensor shares.

    Eden's audio addon runs the usual three-stage pipeline: synthesis (a body turns physics into a block of samples), propagation (the samples travel, attenuating and arriving late), rendering (a microphone sums what reaches it). Sources publish into the registry defined here; microphones render what they find in it, with no knowledge of concrete source types.

    Where this lives is the whole reason the addon needs no Genesis fork. Upstream owns the registry as a scene-level AudioManager, which takes three Genesis edits to exist: Simulator to construct it, Scene.step to pump it, and Scene.add_audio_source to fill it. Genesis already ships a mechanism with exactly those lifecycle hooks — SharedSensorContext, a resource shared across sensor types that SensorManager constructs on first use, refreshes once per step, resets, and destroys. Hosting the registry there gets the same behaviour as a pure addition.

    The ordering that matters comes for free. SensorManager.step calls context.update() before the per-sensor-type update loop, so every source has synthesized the current step's block by the time any microphone renders — whatever order the sensors were declared in. A source that synthesized inside its own sensor's update hook would instead be at the mercy of declaration order, and a microphone declared first would render a block one step stale.

    The delay line lives here for a related but sharper reason: it must advance on every simulation step, and a microphone does not. Eden skips the per-sensor-type update loop on intermediate decimation sub-steps (EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep) while context.update() still runs, so a history advanced from a microphone's render hook would drop every block but the last of each control step — silently shortening every propagation delay. Advancing it here keeps the recorded sound continuous no matter how often anything renders it.

    Classes¶

    AudioSource ¶

    Bases: ABC

    One radiating body in the scene: the synthesis stage of the audio pipeline.

    A source generates sound from physics and is never read by the user — a microphone (:class:~eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio.SpatialAudioSensor) renders it. Subclasses own their sample buffers and expose the radiation interface below so receivers stay decoupled from concrete source types.

    An emission point is one place sound leaves the body: a motor source has one per actuated DOF, a contact source one per contact patch. All three tensors are indexed by that axis.

    Bases: SharedSensorContext

    Registry of :class:AudioSource objects plus the delay line carrying their sound.

    Held by SensorManager as the shared context of the audio sensor classes, so exactly one instance exists per scene however many audio sensors are declared. See the module docstring for why both the registry and the history live here rather than on the scene or on a microphone.

    The delay line is a ring of whole blocks: :meth:update overwrites the oldest block in place, and a reader maps a sample's age to its slot through :attr:hist_newest. Nothing is allocated per step.

    def __init__(self, sim):
    super().__init__(sim)
    self._sources: list[AudioSource] = []
    # The scene-wide sample rate multiplier, adopted from the first participant to declare one.
    # 0 means "not yet claimed"; `require_audio_substeps` fixes it and rejects disagreement.
    self._audio_substeps = 0
    # Delay-line depth in samples requested by the microphones' propagation reach at build.
    self._hist_len = 0
    # (B, n_src, H) ring of samples. The source count is only final once every source has registered, so
    # this and the per-emission-point tensors below are allocated on the first update rather than at build.
    self._src_hist = torch.empty(0)
    self._hist_newest = -1
    self._src_offset = torch.empty(0)
    self._src_is_static = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.bool)
    self._attached_cols = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.long)
    self._attached_links = torch.empty(0, dtype=gs.tc_int)
    # (first emission-point column, source) for every source that radiates.
    self._src_slices: list[tuple[int, AudioSource]] = []
    # Blocks synthesized so far. A consumer remembers the value it last rendered at, which tells it how
    # many blocks it skipped; see `blocks_since`.
    self._n_updates = 0
    self._warned_gapped = False

    def register(self, source: AudioSource, owner: str) -> None:
    """Add ``source`` to the registry and activate it. Call from a producing sensor's ``build``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source : AudioSource
        The source to register. Its ``audio_substeps`` must agree with every other participant.
    owner : str
        Name of the options class that declared the source, for the error message.
    """
    if self._src_hist.numel() > 0:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"{owner} registered an audio source after the delay line was sized for {self._src_hist.shape[1]} "
            "emission points. Register every source at build, before the registry's first update."
        )
    self.require_audio_substeps(source.audio_substeps, owner)
    self._sources.append(source)
    self._active = True

    def require_audio_substeps(self, audio_substeps: int, who: str) -> None:
    """Claim the scene-wide ``audio_substeps``, or fail if it disagrees with the claim on record.

    Sources and microphones exchange fixed-length sample blocks, so one rate has to hold across
    the scene. Checking it here — at build, naming both values — beats discovering a ragged block
    inside the render loop.

    Parameters
    ----------
    audio_substeps : int
        The caller's samples-per-step.
    who : str
        Name of the calling participant, for the error message.
    """
    if self._audio_substeps == 0:
        self._audio_substeps = audio_substeps
    elif self._audio_substeps != audio_substeps:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"{who} declares audio_substeps={audio_substeps} but the scene's audio pipeline is already "
            f"running at audio_substeps={self._audio_substeps}. Every audio source and microphone in a "
            "scene must share one sample rate."
        )

    Manager-driven, once per simulation step, before anything renders.

    def update(self) -> None:
    """Synthesize every source's block and write it over the oldest block of the delay line.

    Manager-driven, once per simulation step, before anything renders.
    """
    if not self._active:
        return
    for source in self._sources:
        source.emit()
    if self._src_hist.numel() == 0 and not self._allocate():
        return

    K = self._audio_substeps
    start = (self._hist_newest + 1) % self._src_hist.shape[2]
    for col, source in self._src_slices:
        n_emit = source.emit_links.shape[0]
        self._src_hist[:, col : col + n_emit, start : start + K] = source.block
        self._src_offset[:, col : col + n_emit] = source.emit_offset
    self._hist_newest = start + K - 1
    self._n_updates += 1

    def source_positions(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``(B, n_src, 3)`` world position of every emission point, parallel to :attr:`src_hist`.

    An emission point rides its link with the offset rotated into the link's frame; a static one sits at its
    offset. Poses are the solver-frame ones (``relative=False``), matching ``eden.entities.sensor.Sensor``.
    """
    self._assert_active("source_positions")
    pos = self._src_offset.clone()
    if self._attached_cols.numel() > 0:
        solver = self._sim.rigid_solver
        links_pos = solver.get_links_pos(links_idx=self._attached_links)
        links_quat = solver.get_links_quat(links_idx=self._attached_links)
        if solver.n_envs == 0:
            links_pos, links_quat = links_pos[None], links_quat[None]
        pos[:, self._attached_cols] = links_pos + transform_by_quat(pos[:, self._attached_cols], links_quat)
    return pos

    Blocks synthesized since a consumer last rendered at n_updates == last_render; warn once if over 1.

That distinction is invisible in the data, and the decimation is Eden's, which a Genesis sensor cannot see at build, so say so on the first gapped render.

    def blocks_since(self, last_render: int, who: str) -> int:
    """Blocks synthesized since a consumer last rendered at ``n_updates == last_render``; warn once if over 1.

    A consumer reads the newest block, so one render per :meth:`update` yields a continuous signal. Eden's
    default ``EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep=False`` skips sensor updates on intermediate decimation
    sub-steps, so with ``decimation=4`` a sensor renders every fourth block and its ``read()`` is a gapped
    stream — fine as an observation, wrong as a recording. That distinction is invisible in the data, and
    the decimation is Eden's, which a Genesis sensor cannot see at build, so say so on the first gapped render.

    Parameters
    ----------
    last_render : int
        :attr:`n_updates` as it stood at the consumer's previous render.
    who : str
        Name of the consuming sensor's options class, for the warning.
    """
    n_blocks = self._n_updates - last_render
    if n_blocks > 1 and not self._warned_gapped:
        self._warned_gapped = True
        en.logger.warning(
            f"{who} is rendered once per {n_blocks} synthesized audio blocks, so read() is a gapped stream "
            "rather than continuous sound. Propagation delay, attenuation and Doppler stay correct (the delay "
            "line advances every step), and this is harmless when the signal is an observation. Set "
            "EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep=True to render every block, e.g. when writing the signal "
            "to an audio file."
        )
    return n_blocks

    def reset(self, envs_idx) -> None:
    """Clear every source's synthesis state and the delay line for ``envs_idx``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    envs_idx : array-like | None
        Environments being reset. ``None`` resets all of them.
    """
    if not self._active:
        return
    for source in self._sources:
        source.reset(envs_idx)
    if self._src_hist.numel() > 0:
        self._src_hist[slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx] = 0.0

    Functions:¶

    Microphone¶

    Airborne point microphone: the rendering stage of the audio pipeline.

    Provenance

    Ported from neuroagents-lab/tactile-genesis @ 3023bcd (Genesis/genesis/engine/sensors/spatial_audio.py), where it is a Genesis in-tree sensor reading a scene-level AudioManager. Here it renders :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext instead, which needs no Genesis change; see :mod:eden.engine.sensors.audio.

    Deviations from upstream: enable_occlusion is dropped (upstream declares it and never reads it); attenuation is a Literal rather than a free str whose typos fell back to inverse; the sample history lives on the context, not the microphone; and the link attachment goes through Genesis' KinematicSensorMixin, so pos_offset is link-local and set_pos_offset works as on any other sensor.

    Limitation: free-field propagation only — no occlusion, no reflections, no room response. A microphone behind a wall hears the source as if the wall were not there.

    Classes¶

    SpatialAudio ¶

    Bases: KinematicSensorOptionsMixin['SpatialAudioSensor'], SimpleSensorOptions['SpatialAudioSensor']

    A mono point microphone that hears every audio source registered with the scene.

    read() returns (B, audio_substeps): this step's block of samples, one microphone signal per environment. Sources are summed with ref_distance-referenced distance attenuation and delayed by distance / speed_of_sound through a fractional delay line.

    PARAMETER DESCRIPTION
    entity_idx

    Global entity index the microphone rides. -1 pins it in the world at pos_offset.

    TYPE: int

    link_idx_local

    Local link index on that entity.

    TYPE: int

    pos_offset

    Microphone position: in the link's frame when attached, world when static.

    TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

    euler_offset

    Accepted for parity with other link-attached sensors; a mono point microphone has no direction, so it does not change what is heard.

    TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

    audio_substeps

    Samples rendered per physics step. Must match every source in the scene; the effective sample rate is audio_substeps / sim_dt.

    TYPE: int

    speed_of_sound

    Propagation speed in m/s, setting the delay per meter. Default 343.0 (air, ~20 °C).

    TYPE: float

    ref_distance

    Distance in meters at which a source is heard at unit gain. Attenuation is clamped closer than this, so a source passing through the microphone stays finite. Default 0.1.

    TYPE: float

    attenuation

    Falloff with distance. 'inverse' is ref/r (sound pressure, the physical free-field law and the usual choice); 'inverse_square' is (ref/r)**2, falling off faster.

    TYPE: (inverse, inverse_square) DEFAULT: 'inverse'

    enable_doppler

    Ramp delay and attenuation across each block from last step's value to this step's, which pitch-shifts a source in relative motion. Costs nothing extra; disable for a static rig.

    TYPE: bool

    max_delay

    Longest propagation delay to keep history for, in seconds. Sources farther than max_delay * speed_of_sound are heard at that clamped delay rather than their true one. Sizes the delay line, so raise it only as far as the scene needs. Default 0.03 (~10 m).

    TYPE: float

    Examples:

    A microphone on a robot's head, hearing its own motors:

    >>> from eden.options import SensorOptions
>>> from eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio import SpatialAudio
>>> mic = SensorOptions(
...     sensor=SpatialAudio(audio_substeps=20, ref_distance=0.2),
...     attach_entity_name="robot",
...     attach_link_name="head_link",
... )

    SpatialAudioSensor(options: SpatialAudio, idx: int, shared_context: AudioContext, shared_metadata: SpatialAudioSensorMetadata, manager: SensorManager)

    Bases: KinematicSensorMixin, SimpleSensor[SpatialAudio, AudioContext, SpatialAudioSensorMetadata]

    Renders :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext into one microphone signal per listener.

    For each (listener, source) pair the current distance gives an attenuation and a delay in samples; the delay indexes the per-source sample history with linear interpolation between the two straddling samples, and the results are summed over sources. Interpolating the delay across the block from its value one simulation step ago to its current one is what produces Doppler: a shrinking delay reads the history faster than real time, raising the pitch.

    def build(self):
    """Claim the scene's sample rate and append this listener's column."""
    super().build()

    sm = self._shared_metadata
    context = self._shared_context
    # A microphone alone in the scene is valid (it renders silence), so activate rather than
    # register: activation is what a *consumer* of the registry declares.
    context.activate()
    context.require_audio_substeps(self._options.audio_substeps, type(self._options).__name__)

    sm.speed_of_sound = concat_with_tensor(sm.speed_of_sound, self._options.speed_of_sound)
    sm.ref_distance = concat_with_tensor(sm.ref_distance, self._options.ref_distance)
    sm.inverse_square = concat_with_tensor(sm.inverse_square, self._options.attenuation == "inverse_square")
    sm.doppler = concat_with_tensor(sm.doppler, self._options.enable_doppler)

    K = self._options.audio_substeps
    if sm.ramp.numel() == 0:
        sm.ramp = (torch.arange(1, K + 1, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float) / K).view(1, 1, 1, K)
        sm.age = torch.arange(K - 1, -1, -1, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float).view(1, 1, 1, K)

    # The delay line must span this listener's longest delay plus the block it renders.
    dt_sub = self._manager._sim.dt / K
    delay_samples = int(self._options.max_delay / dt_sub) + 2
    context.require_history(K + delay_samples)
